```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
A <- "docs/assets/fdr_reads10"
ov <- fread(file.path(A, "fdr_overview.tsv"))
vp <- fread(file.path(A, "overview_vs_panel10.tsv"))
rounds <- fread(file.path(A, "adaptive_rounds.tsv"))
cons <- fread(file.path(A, "consistency.tsv"))
g <- fread(file.path(A, "significant_genes.tsv"))
gc <- fread(file.path(A, "gene_changes.tsv"))
fs <- fread(file.path(A, "fate_summary.tsv"))
fd <- fread(file.path(A, "fate_direction.tsv"))
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
pct <- function(x, digits=0) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), 100 * x)
counts <- function(a, b) sprintf("%s (%s)", fmt(a), fmt(b))
any_tp <- ov[tp == "any timepoint"]; any_vp <- vp[tp == "any timepoint"]
effect_reads <- function(d, t) fifelse(is.na(d[[paste0("dpsi_", t)]]), "no score",
  sprintf("%+.0f (%s)", 100 * d[[paste0("dpsi_", t)]], fmt(d[[paste0("het_cov_", t)]])))
best_q <- function(d) signif(pmin(d$q_bh_0hr, d$q_bh_1hr, d$q_bh_6hr, na.rm=TRUE), 2)
example_table <- function(genes, why) {
  d <- g[match(genes, gene)]
  data.table(Gene=d$gene, `0 hr`=effect_reads(d, "0hr"), `1 hr`=effect_reads(d, "1hr"), `6 hr`=effect_reads(d, "6hr"),
             `Best q`=best_q(d), `Het donors`=d$max_het, Relevance=why)
}
pattern_labels <- c("all three timepoints"="Significant at 3 timepoints",
                    "two timepoints"="Significant at 2 timepoints",
                    "shared, below threshold elsewhere"="One timepoint; nominal support elsewhere",
                    "candidate timepoint-specific"="One timepoint; no nominal support elsewhere",
                    "not testable elsewhere"="One timepoint; no usable score elsewhere")
g[, display_pattern := unname(pattern_labels[pattern])]
annot <- function(d) d[, .(`Neuronal GO term`=neuronal_go,
  `Developmental disorder or autism`=fifelse(nzchar(sfari) & nzchar(ddg2p), paste0(sfari, "; ", ddg2p), paste0(sfari, ddg2p)),
  `Expression after stimulation`=expression_response, `Splicing after stimulation`=fifelse(stim_splicing, "yes", ""))]
interactive_table <- function(d) DT::datatable(as.data.frame(d), rownames=FALSE, filter="top", extensions="Buttons",
  options=list(pageLength=10, lengthMenu=c(10, 25, 50), scrollX=TRUE, order=list(), dom="Blfrtip", buttons=c("copy", "csv")),
  caption="Search or filter genes, sort columns, and export the filtered table as CSV.")
both_genes <- gc[status == "both", gene]; p10_only <- gc[status == "panel10 only", gene]; r10_only <- gc[status == "reads10 only", gene]
f_of <- function(run, st) fs[reported_in == run & status == st]
n_rep <- function(run) fs[reported_in == run, sum(associations)]
dir_of <- function(run) fd[reported_in == run]
```

> **Earlier setup.** This page keeps the clustering filter, which the current
> analyses drop. Current pages: [read-based isoLASER](isolaser_fdr_reads10nc.html)
> (main analysis) and [transcript-based isoLASER](isolaser_fdr_panel10nc.html).


This page repeats [transcript-based isoLASER](isolaser_fdr_panel10.html) with
one change: **each read's inclusion label comes from its own alignment.** The
transcript-based page and its results are unchanged.

**What changed (our definitions):**

- **How isoLASER labels reads:** isoLASER decides whether a read includes or
  excludes an exonic part from the transcript the read was assigned to, not from
  the read's own alignment. A read assigned to a transcript that retains an
  intron counts as retaining it, even if the read splices it out. For example,
  isoLASER counted 28 ALT reads as keeping the tested KPNA2 intron of the transcript-based
  page; in their alignments, 20 of them splice it out (our read check).
- **Read-based labels:** a modified copy of isoLASER labels each read from its
  alignment. A read **includes** the part if at least 10 of its aligned bases
  fall inside it (all of them, for parts shorter than 10 bases), and
  **excludes** it if one of its splice junctions spans the whole part. Other
  reads (those that don't reach the part) get no label and are not counted.
  Variant calls, phasing and allele assignments are unchanged: every read keeps
  the allele it had in the original run.
- **Unchanged from the transcript-based run:** panel-heterozygous donors with ≥ 10
  reads, every recorded variant × exonic part, the tested family (≥ 20 reads over
  the donors used, part ≥ 10 bp, and no other candidate variant within 30 bp),
  the shuffles, isoLASER's scoring functions, the adaptive rounds, BH within each
  timepoint, and the `cis` / |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10 screen.
- **Checks:** the modified run's allele assignments match the original run's
  exactly, on all 66 chromosome × timepoint combinations. The unshuffled score of
  every tested association was rebuilt independently, from isoLASER's own summary
  tables, and matched.
- **Not yet done:** calibration runs.

**Main result:** `r fmt(any_tp$q05_associations)` associations in
**`r fmt(any_tp$q05_genes)` genes** have q < 0.05 and pass the screen,
against `r fmt(any_vp$panel10_q05_associations)` in
`r fmt(any_vp$panel10_q05_genes)` genes in the transcript-based run.
`r length(both_genes)` genes are reported in both. The reported effects of the
transcript-based run mostly vanish with read-based labels, while this run's effects
are already visible, in the same direction, in the transcript-based run
([details](#what-happened-to-each-runs-reported-associations)).

# Genome-wide results

```{r overview}
knitr::kable(ov[, .(Timepoint=tp, `Tested associations`=fmt(tested),
  `Paper's cutoff`=counts(paper_associations, paper_genes),
  Screen=counts(screen_associations, screen_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.10`=counts(q10_associations, q10_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.05`=counts(q05_associations, q05_genes))], align="lrrrrr")
```

Cells other than **Tested associations** show **associations (genes)**.

- **Paper's cutoff:** isoLASER's own `cis` call with no other filter, as in the
  isoLASER paper. Here it comes from the joint output of the read-based run, so it
  differs from the transcript-based page's.
- **Screen** (our definition), before FDR control: among the tested
  associations, isoLASER's `cis` rule computed on the panel-heterozygous donors
  only, plus |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10.

**Any timepoint** counts each gene or variant–part association once across
timepoints. BH targets FDR within each timepoint's full family; the
effect-filtered subset and the union across timepoints have no separate 5% FDR
guarantee.

# Compared with the transcript-based run

```{r vs_panel10}
knitr::kable(vp[, .(Timepoint=tp,
  `Tested: transcript-based`=fmt(panel10_tested), `Tested: read-based`=fmt(tested),
  `Paper's cutoff: transcript-based`=counts(panel10_paper_associations, panel10_paper_genes),
  `Paper's cutoff: read-based`=counts(paper_associations, paper_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.05: transcript-based`=counts(panel10_q05_associations, panel10_q05_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.05: read-based`=counts(q05_associations, q05_genes))], align="lrrrrrr")
```

**Transcript-based** and **read-based** are the two isoLASER versions, both with the clustering filter; this page is read-based. About half as
many associations are testable. Many reads were counted only because of their
assigned transcript and never reach the part; they are no longer counted, so
fewer associations have 20 reads.

## What happened to each run's reported associations

Each reported association (at its timepoint) is looked up in the other run, at
the same timepoint:

```{r fate}
ST <- c("reported", "q < 0.05, fails the screen", "tested, q >= 0.05", "tested, no observed score", "under 20 labelled reads",
        "part under 10 bp or a nearby variant", "no heterozygous donor with 10 labelled reads", "not recorded")
lab <- c("reported"="Reported", "q < 0.05, fails the screen"="q < 0.05, fails the screen",
         "tested, q >= 0.05"="Tested, q ≥ 0.05", "tested, no observed score"="Tested, no score",
         "under 20 labelled reads"="Not tested: under 20 reads",
         "part under 10 bp or a nearby variant"="Not tested: part under 10 bp or a nearby variant",
         "no heterozygous donor with 10 labelled reads"="Not tested: no heterozygous donor with 10 reads",
         "not recorded"="Not recorded: no read labelled")
w <- dcast(fs, status ~ reported_in, value.var="associations", fill=0)
w <- w[order(match(status, ST))]
knitr::kable(w[, .(`In the other run`=unname(lab[status]), `Reported transcript-based, looked up read-based`=panel10,
                   `Reported read-based, looked up transcript-based`=reads10)], align="lrr")
```

Counts are association × timepoint rows: an association reported at two
timepoints counts twice. **Not recorded**: no donor has a read labelled for this
variant × part. With read-based labels this means no read reaches the part with
10 aligned bases or a spanning junction.

```{r fate_direction}
knitr::kable(fd[match(c("panel10", "reads10"), reported_in), .(`Reported in`=c(panel10="transcript-based", reads10="read-based")[reported_in],
  `Tested in both`=pairs, `Same direction`=pct(same_sign),
  `Median |ΔPSI|, reporting run`=sprintf("%.3f", median_abs_dpsi),
  `Median |ΔPSI|, other run`=sprintf("%.3f", median_abs_other_dpsi))], align="lrrrr")
```

**Tested in both**: reported in one run and scored in the other at the same
timepoint. **Same direction**: the ΔPSI has the same sign in both runs.

The two directions of the comparison look very different:

- **Transcript-based reported associations** mostly fall apart with read-based labels.
  Only `r f_of("panel10", "reported")$associations` of
  `r n_rep("panel10")` are reported again. Where both runs score them, the
  direction agrees in `r pct(dir_of("panel10")$same_sign)` (chance level), and
  the median effect drops from `r sprintf("%.2f", dir_of("panel10")$median_abs_dpsi)`
  to `r sprintf("%.3f", dir_of("panel10")$median_abs_other_dpsi)`. Their effects
  came from the transcripts the reads were assigned to, not from the reads.
- **This run's reported associations** are visible in the transcript-based run too: same
  direction in `r pct(dir_of("reads10")$same_sign)`, with a smaller median effect
  (`r sprintf("%.2f", dir_of("reads10")$median_abs_other_dpsi)` against
  `r sprintf("%.2f", dir_of("reads10")$median_abs_dpsi)`). Transcript-based
  labels diluted them below significance.

**Genes.** Reported in both: `r paste(both_genes, collapse=", ")`.
Transcript-based only: `r paste(p10_only, collapse=", ")`. This run only:
`r paste(r10_only, collapse=", ")`.
[Download the gene comparison](assets/fdr_reads10/gene_changes.tsv), or every
reported association with its status in the other run:
[transcript-based's](assets/fdr_reads10/fate_panel10_reported.tsv),
[this run's](assets/fdr_reads10/fate_reads10_reported.tsv).

# How the test works

The test is the one described on the [original page](isolaser_fdr.html#how-the-test-works),
with the donor and family rules of the [transcript-based run](isolaser_fdr_panel10.html).
Only the read labels differ.

```{r rounds}
knitr::kable(rounds[, .(Timepoint=tp, `Stopped at 1,000`=fmt(stopped_1e3),
  `Stopped at 10,000`=fmt(stopped_1e4), `Stopped at 100,000`=fmt(stopped_1e5),
  `Reached 1,000,000`=fmt(reached_1e6))], align="lrrrr")
```

**Stopped** means at least 20 hits at that checkpoint, or no observed score
(p = 1). Every association with zero hits after a million shuffles has
q < 0.05, so more shuffles would not change the results.

![](assets/fdr_reads10/qq.png)

Real data only; there are no calibration runs for this run. As in the transcript-based run, the
bulk lies below the diagonal (many ties at an AMI of 0) and the upper plateau is
the minimum attainable p-value.

# Genes to follow up

```{r follow_setup}
sashimi <- fread(file.path(A, "sashimi_summary.tsv"))
sashimi_table <- function(gn) {
  d <- sashimi[gene == gn][order(timepoint)]
  frac <- function(i, e) sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", i, i + e, 100 * i / (i + e))
  knitr::kable(d[, .(Timepoint=sub("hr", " hr", timepoint), Donors=donors,
    `REF inclusion (raw)`=frac(REF_i, REF_e), `ALT inclusion (raw)`=frac(ALT_i, ALT_e),
    `Test dPSI (normalized, pp)`=sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * normalized_dPSI))], align="llrrr")
}
n_two <- g[!grepl("0hr", sig_tps) & (neuronal | brain_disorder | stim_expression | stim_splicing), .N]
```

We highlight genes that meet the same two conditions as on the
[transcript-based page](isolaser_fdr_panel10.html#genes-to-follow-up) (our definitions):

1. **Reported only after stimulation:** q < 0.05 plus the `cis` /
   effect-size screen at 1 or 6 hours, and not at 0 hours.
2. **Neuron- or stimulation-related:** a neuronal GO term, a disorder in SFARI
   or DDG2P, or a change in expression or splicing after stimulation in our data
   (the annotation columns of the full gene table below).

`r n_two` genes meet both; four are shown. Not shown: **C20orf96** and
**ENSG00000290928**, which have no score at 0 hours, so there is no 0-hour
comparison. PARK7 and ZNF749 are also on the transcript-based page; PPA2 and LY6H are new.

```{r highlight}
knitr::kable(example_table(c("PARK7", "PPA2", "LY6H", "ZNF749"), c(
  "Neuron projection, neuron death (GO); the Parkinson's disease gene DJ-1",
  "Splicing after stimulation (our scan); a GTEx Cerebellum sQTL for this exon",
  "Synaptic signaling (GO)",
  "Splicing after stimulation (our scan), at this exon's donor sites")), align="lrrrrrl")
```

**0 / 1 / 6 hr**: allelic effect in percentage points, alternative minus
reference inclusion, with pooled informative coverage in brackets. **Best q**:
the lowest timepoint-specific q-value. **Het donors**: the largest number of
panel-heterozygous donors used, out of four. All numbers refer to each gene's
representative association.

**How to read each gene's figures:**

- **Permutation test:** one panel per timepoint. Grey bars are the first 1,000
  shuffled scores; the blue line is the observed score (AMI). The p-value uses
  the full adaptive run, up to a million shuffles.
- **Read alignments:** isoLASER's `nigiri_plot` sashimi renderer with the
  project's plotting fixes. Reads are split into REF (blue) and ALT (orange) and
  pooled over the donors used at each timepoint. Yellow marks the tested part.
  Coverage and arc numbers are raw read counts, on one scale per gene. **Raw
  inclusion** is each read's own label, so every counted read reaches the part;
  these are the counts the test uses before it normalizes donors.
- **Isoforms and haplotypes**, at 0 hours and at the significant timepoint,
  drawn as on the transcript-based page:
  - **Rows:** the transcripts the reads were assigned to, grouped by whether the
    transcript's structure includes the part. With read-based labels, a read's
    own label can differ from its transcript's group.
  - **Numbers:** reads per transcript from each haplotype, raw counts summed
    over the donors used.
  - **PSI row:** each haplotype's inclusion from the reads' own labels, the
    raw version of the test's table. A note under the row gives any reads assigned
    to transcripts that don't span the part: they count in PSI but are not drawn.
  - **Test line:** the test's ΔPSI and q.

## PARK7

The tested 46-base part is the extra stretch of PARK7-201's longer first exon.
Its donor site lies 58 bases beyond the other transcripts' donor site, an
alternative 5′ splice site; the transcript-based page tested the adjacent 12-base part of
the same stretch. One minor transcript (ENST00000465354) has this part as its
whole first exon, which is why the figure's automatic label reads "alternative first exon".

ALT (C) reads use the longer first exon less often than REF (T) reads. The effect
has the same direction at all three timepoints and in both donors (CD_21 and
CD_48), and is largest at 1 hour: −19 pp (q = 0.002), with REF 74% vs ALT 51% and
REF 73% vs ALT 57% in the two donors. At 0 and 6 hours it is −8 and −10 pp. The variant
(rs226249) lies in the first exon, 18 bases before the shorter exon's donor
site.

## PPA2

PPA2 encodes the mitochondrial inorganic pyrophosphatase. DDG2P lists a
PPA2-related sudden cardiac death disorder, which is not a brain disorder. The
tested 27-base part is the last stretch of an 87-base cassette exon. PPA2-202
skips the whole exon, and the reads that exclude the part skip the whole exon:
none use the exon's shorter form.

ALT (G) reads include the exon more often than REF (C) reads. The effect is
largest at 1 hour: +46 pp (q = 0.004), from REF 33% vs ALT 77% raw inclusion, with +53
and +36 pp in the two donors (CD_31 and CD_48). At 0 and 6 hours it is +21 and
+18 pp, below threshold; CD_36, with 6 to 16 reads per allele, varies between
−5 and +12 pp. The tested SNP (rs13787) is in a downstream exon, about 42 kb
away in the genome. GTEx Cerebellum has a strong sQTL at the same SNP for this
exon's skipping junction (p = 1 × 10⁻¹⁹), with the opposite sign to our ΔPSI,
as expected ([GTEx page](isolaser_gtex_comparison_reads10.html)).

## LY6H

The tested 12-base part is the start of LY6H-201's first exon. LY6H-202 and
LY6H-205 start at an exon further upstream and splice past the part into an exon
inside LY6H-201's first exon. Read coverage ends at LY6H-201's start site, so
reads that include the part start there, and reads that exclude it splice from
the upstream exon. The test therefore compares the use of two first exons (our
reading of the alignments and annotation).

ALT (G) reads include the part more often than REF (A) reads, so they use the
upstream first exon less. The effect has the same direction at all three
timepoints and in both donors (CD_21 and CD_31), and is largest at 6 hours:
+25 pp (q = 0.001), from REF 66% vs ALT 92% raw inclusion, with +30 and +20 pp in the two
donors. At 0 and 1 hours it is +15 and +14 pp, below threshold. The tested SNP
(rs10109061) is in the last exon, 1.9 kb from the part. LY6H belongs to the Ly6
family of GPI-anchored, neurotoxin-like proteins. Published work (not our data)
reports that it limits surface α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in neurons.

## ZNF749

As on the transcript-based page, the tested part is a 355-base alternative last exon.
REF (G) reads end in it far more often than ALT (C) reads. The difference is
significant only at 6 hours (−74 pp, q = 0.001); at 0 and 1 hours it is −26 and
−8 pp. In our stimulation splicing scan, the balance between the two donor sites
that splice into this exon shifts between 0 and 6 hours.

As before, the jump at 6 hours partly reflects which donors are used:

- **CD_21** has a large effect at every timepoint: −72, −43 and −81 pp.
- **CD_48** shows no difference at 0 hours (+1 pp, from 8 ALT reads) and a large
  one at 6 hours (−66 pp).
- **CD_36** has an inconsistent effect (−19 pp at 0 hours, +18 pp at 1 hour)
  and no reads at 6 hours.

# All reported genes

Here, **reported** means q < 0.05 plus the `cis` / effect-size screen.

```{r patterns}
pat <- g[, .N, by=pattern][match(names(pattern_labels), pattern)][!is.na(pattern)]
knitr::kable(pat[, .(Pattern=unname(pattern_labels[pattern]), Genes=N)], align="lr")
```

For genes reported at one timepoint, the last three categories describe the
representative association at the other timepoints: nominal p < 0.05,
p ≥ 0.05 where scored, or no usable score. They are not tests of an allele ×
time interaction. Among comparisons of significant associations with another
timepoint, `r pct(cons$nominal_p_lt_0.05)` had nominal p < 0.05 there and
`r pct(cons$same_sign)` had the same effect direction.

## Full interactive gene table

All **`r nrow(g)` reported genes**. The variant, part, timepoint effects, best q
and donor count refer to the representative association; **Significant at**
describes the gene across all its associations. **In transcript-based** marks genes also
reported in the transcript-based run.

```{r all}
interactive_table(cbind(g[, .(Gene=gene, Pattern=display_pattern, `Significant at`=sig_tps,
  `0 hr`=effect_reads(g, "0hr"), `1 hr`=effect_reads(g, "1hr"), `6 hr`=effect_reads(g, "6hr"),
  `Best q`=best_q(g), `Het donors`=max_het,
  `In transcript-based`=fifelse(gene %in% both_genes, "yes", "no"))], annot(g),
  g[, .(Variant=variant_qual, `Exonic part`=exonic_part)]))
```

**0 / 1 / 6 hr**: allelic effect in percentage points, alternative minus
reference inclusion, with pooled informative coverage in brackets. The
annotations use the same rules as on the
[original page](isolaser_fdr.html#full-interactive-gene-table). They help select
examples and are not enrichment tests.

**Data:** `10.isolaser_permutation/` with `ADAPTIVE_RULE=reads10`: the
read-based isoLASER run from `40.make_reads_copy.py` and
`41.reads_record.sbatch` / `42.reads_joint.sbatch`, checked by
`43.check_reads_record.py`; inputs from `38.prepare_panel_inputs.R`, then
scripts 18–22, with the independent score check `48` / `50`. This page's tables
come from `11.fdr_results/3.page_tables.R` with `ADAPTIVE_RULE=reads10`, which
writes only to `docs/assets/fdr_reads10/`.
